subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should issue #48874 remain the umbrella for multi-session architecture, or should maintainers split its remaining work into narrower canonical issues for routing identity, WebUI session lifecycle, topic-session families, and shared-memory security?
rationale: Current main partially implements the requested primitives, but the missing behavior changes product architecture, compatibility, and security boundaries rather than one broken code path.

options.title: Split Into Staged Design Issues
options.body: Keep this RFC open until maintainers choose canonical sub-issues and owners for routing, UI lifecycle, topic-family semantics, and memory/RAG security.

options.title: Use Topic Families As Canonical
options.body: Move the state-model portion to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90916 and keep only routing/UI/security leftovers here.

options.title: Sponsor Broad Rewrite
options.body: Approve a coordinated architecture project across routing, storage, UI, and memory with explicit migration and security review before implementation PRs.

recommendation.title: Split Into Staged Design Issues
recommendation.body: Keep this RFC open until maintainers choose canonical sub-issues and owners for routing, UI lifecycle, topic-family semantics, and memory/RAG security.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core session routing, gateway APIs, UI lifecycle, and security posture, and Peter has the strongest recent session-organization ownership signal.
